key_insight: A multilayer neural network can learn the mapping from modal design parameters to cascaded-mode near-field landscapes and enable inverse design of target optical field profiles.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route to engineer structured near-fields for microscopy and nanoparticle manipulation without relying solely on manual modal coefficient tuning.
method: Model the forward relationship between design parameters and near-field patterns with multilayer neural networks.
Use gradient-based optimization on the trained network to reconstruct target longitudinal and lateral field profiles.
Improve lateral reconstruction by selecting and augmenting training data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate prediction for simple and complex longitudinal landscapes, with lateral field reconstruction improving after data selection and augmentation.
watch_item: Lateral field inverse design remains harder than longitudinal design, so performance may depend strongly on training data quality and coverage.
paper_title: Neural Networks for Inverse Design of Cascaded-Mode Near-Field Landscapes
